suite.name: Rx

kw.name: Open Bench
kw.msg: Set suite metadata 'Radio' to value 'Connect Systems CS7000-PLUS (cs7000p)'.
Set suite metadata 'Calibration' to value 'assumed, measured 2026-10-20 (d55ce4aa0a3c)'.
Set suite metadata 'Suite commit' to value 'be862b1ada'.
kw.doc: Load the bench, its calibration and the radio file, and prepare the instruments. All five are mandatory and differ from tester to tester, so suites take them from the command line (-v BENCH:... and so on). `firmware` names what the radio runs, such as a git describe; `hardware` names the unit, by model and serial number, since units of one model measure differently. `dsp` names the DSP image the radio's audio processor runs, such as its sha256; it is mandatory for radio files with dsp_image: true, whose firmware states can differ in it alone.

test.name: 70cm: M17 RX Shows The Callsign

kw.name: Use Band
kw.doc: Make a band from the radio file current: captures and transmissions use its frequency. Sets ${BAND} and ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} for the test. oat.expand calls it in each per-band test's setup.

kw.name: Set Radio Volume Once
kw.msg: Set suite metadata 'Radio volume' to value 'knob 3 pm'.
kw.doc: Have the operator set the radio's volume for the receive tests that record its speaker, once per run, and record the setting. Later calls return the first setting.

kw.name: Operator Does
kw.arg: Set the radio to M17, ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} MHz, no encryption, any destination accepted, volume unchanged
kw.doc: Ask the operator to do something and wait until it's done.

kw.name: Start Transmitting M17 Stream
kw.doc: Loop an M17 voice stream on the test frequency until stopped: preamble, LSF from `source` to `destination`, stream frames, EOT, then gap_s without carrier, so the radio sees separate transmissions. `audio` is tone:<Hz> or tone:<Hz>:<dBFS> (Codec2, `frames` long), a WAV file (Codec2, its whole length), or random (random payload bytes, for decoding without Codec2). offset_hz moves the carrier off the channel; inverted sends the symbols with the wrong sign; level_dbm sets the level at the radio's antenna port. With loop=False the stream plays once.

kw.name: Operator Confirms
kw.arg: Each transmission shows ${SOURCE} and plays a steady tone
kw.doc: Ask the operator a yes/no question; fail the test on no.

test.doc: M17-RX-1: the generated stream decodes on the radio.

kw.name: Close Bench
kw.doc: Stop the instruments and write measurements.json: every capture, check and operator answer, with the run's provenance. Absolute paths are made relative, so the file can be published as it is.

suite.doc:
M17 on receive: the transmitter plays a generated voice stream (oat.m17: preamble, LSF from OAT1, stream frames carrying a Codec2 tone, EOT, looped with a gap) and the radio must show the callsign and play the tone. With the audio interface the speaker is measured; without it the operator listens.
Generating the Codec2 tone needs c2enc (the codec2 package).
